messages.subject: RI CLPM 2groups 5time points
parts:
Dear colleagues,

I would appreciate your feedback and advice on the specification of the RI CLPM for 2 groups.


I have two groups of MZ and DZ twins (~1000 individuals in each group) measured more than 5 times for two phenotypes: subjective health (she) and life satisfaction (gls). I want to examine the cross-lagged associations across time for these two groups.

I have to take into account that 1) data is clustered 2) MZ and DZ twins can have different loadings 3) there are also control variables.


What I struggle with:

  1. The model stops converging after adding the fourth time point. I believe this is due to model complexity and small sample size. Currently, I am thinking of running separate models for timepoints (tp) 1, 2, and 3, and then a separate model for tp 2, 3, and 4.  Is this solution feasible? Should I then "just" specify estimated loadings and intercepts from the model with tp 1,2,3 as starting values (or just values) in the model with tp 2,3, and 4?
  2. The model stops converging when I have restrictions for the control variables (sex, age, etc. ) to set the error to zero. It feels that with two groups and control variables, we should have enough pieces of information to measure the model even without this restriction; therefore, I removed it. Does it make sense?
  3. Do I understand correctly that specification of the model within 2 groups will allow me to run the analysis keeping 2 separate variance-covariance matrices? If I have more degrees of freedom in one group (more restrictions), can this information be used to estimate the parameters in the model with fewer degrees of freedom in another group?
  4. Allowing different intercepts across groups. I can specify the different loadings for the regressive pathways for two phenotypes, but I struggle to set different intercepts, as they are all restricted to make the model identifiable. 


model: 

riclpm_3tp <- '

# Define intercept factors
i_gls =~ 1*gls_lv_ad_1+1*gls_lv_ad_2+1*gls_lv_ad_3
i_she =~ 1*she0100_comb_1+1*she0100_comb_2+1*she0100_comb_3

i_gls ~ sex + age0100_scaled_1

# Define single item latent variables
eta_gls1 =~ 1*gls_lv_ad_1+urbanicity_scaled_1+yeduc_scaled_1+hh_inc_scaled_1
eta_gls2 =~ 1*gls_lv_ad_2+urbanicity_scaled_2+yeduc_scaled_2+hh_inc_scaled_2
eta_gls3 =~ 1*gls_lv_ad_3+urbanicity_scaled_3+yeduc_scaled_3+hh_inc_scaled_3

eta_she1 =~ 1*she0100_comb_1
eta_she2 =~ 1*she0100_comb_2
eta_she3 =~ 1*she0100_comb_3

# Autoregressive effects
eta_gls2 ~ c(a1,a2)*eta_gls1
eta_gls3 ~ c(a1,a2)*eta_gls2

eta_she2 ~ c(a1,a2)*eta_she1
eta_she3 ~ c(a1,a2)*eta_she2

# Crosslagged effects

eta_she2 ~ c(m1,m2)*eta_gls1 #start(c(1.2, 0.6))
eta_she3 ~ c(m1,m2)*eta_gls2

eta_gls2 ~ c(m1,m2)*eta_she1
eta_gls3 ~ c(m1,m2)*eta_she2

# Some further constraints on the variance structure

# 1. Set error variances of the observed variables to zero
gls_lv_ad_1 ~~ 0*gls_lv_ad_1
gls_lv_ad_2 ~~ 0*gls_lv_ad_2
gls_lv_ad_3 ~~ 0*gls_lv_ad_3

she0100_comb_1 ~~ 0*she0100_comb_1
she0100_comb_2 ~~ 0*she0100_comb_2
she0100_comb_3 ~~ 0*she0100_comb_3

# 2. Let lavaan estimate the variance of the latent variables
eta_gls1 ~~ vargls1*eta_gls1
eta_gls2 ~~ vargls2*eta_gls2
eta_gls3 ~~ vargls3*eta_gls3

eta_she1 ~~ varshe1*eta_she1
eta_she2 ~~ varshe2*eta_she2
eta_she3 ~~ varshe3*eta_she3

# 3. We also want estimates of the intercept factor variances and an
#    estimate of their covariance
i_gls ~~ varigls*i_gls
i_she ~~ varishe*i_she
i_gls ~~ covi*i_she

# 4. We have to define that the covariance between the intercepts and
#    the latents of the first time point are zero

eta_gls1 ~~ 0*i_gls
eta_she1 ~~ 0*i_gls
eta_gls1 ~~ 0*i_she
eta_she1 ~~ 0*i_she

# 5. Finally, we estimate the covariance between the latents of x and y
#    of the first time point, the second time-point and so on. note that
#    for the second to fourth time point the correlation is constrained to
#    the same value

eta_gls1 ~~ cov1*eta_she1
eta_gls2 ~~ e1*eta_she2
eta_gls3 ~~ e1*eta_she3

# The model also contains a mean structure and we have to define some
# constraints for this part of the model. the assumption is that we
# only want estimates of the mean of the intercept factors. all other means
# are defined to be zero:
gls_lv_ad_1 ~ 0*1
gls_lv_ad_2 ~ 0*1
gls_lv_ad_3 ~ 0*1

she0100_comb_1 ~ 0*1
she0100_comb_2 ~ 0*1
she0100_comb_3 ~ 0*1

sex ~ 0.5*1
age0100_scaled_1 ~ 0*1

urbanicity_scaled_1 ~ 0*1
urbanicity_scaled_2 ~ 0*1
urbanicity_scaled_3 ~ 0*1

yeduc_scaled_1 ~ 0*1
yeduc_scaled_2 ~ 0*1
yeduc_scaled_3 ~ 0*1

hh_inc_scaled_1 ~ 0*1
hh_inc_scaled_2 ~ 0*1
hh_inc_scaled_3 ~ 0*1

eta_gls1 ~ 1
eta_gls2 ~ 1
eta_gls3 ~ 1

eta_she1 ~ 1
eta_she2 ~ 1
eta_she3 ~ 1

i_gls ~ 1
i_she ~ 1

## define correlations
cori := covi / (sqrt(varigls) * sqrt(varishe))
cor1 := cov1 / (sqrt(vargls1) * sqrt(varshe1))
cort2 := e1 / (sqrt(vargls2) * sqrt(varshe2))
cort3 := e1 / (sqrt(vargls3) * sqrt(varshe3))
'

riclpm_fit<- sem(riclpm_3tp, cluster = "fid", group = "zyg",data=df,mimic = "Mplus", missing = "FIML")

thank you in advance!
